bull.b: Accelerating product revenue, strong retention, and expanding customer additions indicate broadening platform adoption. These trends can support durable growth as customers deploy more workloads, increase consumption, and expand Snowflake across additional teams and use cases.

bull.t: Strong cash generation and software economics
bull.b: Robust operating and free cash flow provide internal funding for product development, AI investment, and customer expansion. High gross margins also demonstrate attractive software economics, giving Snowflake a foundation to improve profitability as revenue scales.

Higher revenue and margin guidance signals management sees sustained demand and improving operating leverage. The combination of faster growth and expanding planned margins strengthens the medium-term earnings trajectory, provided execution keeps pace with product adoption.

bear.b: Ongoing operating and net losses show that strong revenue growth has not yet translated into GAAP profitability. Continued losses can constrain retained capital, reduce resilience during slower consumption periods, and leave the company dependent on future operating leverage.

Higher leverage increases the claims on future cash generation and reduces financial flexibility compared with earlier periods. Because annual operating cash flow covers only a modest portion of debt, deleveraging would take time and could limit capital-allocation options.

AI adoption can expand platform usage and revenue, but lower AI gross margins may dilute the economics of the core business as these workloads scale. If infrastructure efficiencies do not offset costs, margin expansion and the path to profitability could be slower.
